Document Accession #: 20260803-3037           Filed Date: 08/03/2026




                                      196 FERC ¶ 61,100
                                 UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                          FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

         Before Commissioners: Laura V. Swett, Chairman;
                               David Rosner, Lindsay S. See,
                               Judy W. Chang, and David LaCerte.

         Digi Power X Inc. f/k/a Digihost Technology Inc.             Docket No. IN25-4-000

                ORDER APPROVING STIPULATION AND CONSENT AGREEMENT

                                          (Issued August 3, 2026)

         1.     The Commission approves the attached Stipulation and Consent Agreement
         (Agreement) between the Office of Enforcement and Regulatory Accounting
         (Enforcement) and Digi Power X Inc. f/k/a Digihost Technology Inc. (Digihost). This
         order is in the public interest because the Agreement resolves on fair and equitable terms
         Enforcement’s investigation (Investigation) under Part 1b of the Commission’s
         regulations, 18 C.F.R. Part 1b (2025), into whether Digihost violated the New York
         Independent System Operator (NYISO) Open Access Transmission Tariff (Tariff)
         Section 3.9.1 from February 17, 2022 to April 30, 2022 (Relevant Period) when Digihost
         interconnected its cryptocurrency load to the Fortistar North Tonawanda LLC (FNT) co-
         generation facility (Facility) without first submitting the required interconnection
         proposal to NYISO.

         2.     Digihost stipulates to the facts in Section II of the Agreement, but neither admits
         nor denies the alleged violation in Section III of the Agreement. Digihost agrees to: (a)
         pay a civil penalty of $45,000 to the United States Treasury; and (b) provide compliance
         monitoring reports to Enforcement as provided in the Agreement.

         I.     Facts

         3.     FNT owned and operated a 55 MW co-generation facility located in North
         Tonawanda, New York that is interconnected to the 115kV transmission system of
         Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation d/b/a National Grid. In March 2021, Digihost
         signed an agreement to purchase FNT from North Tonawanda Holdings, LLC (North
         Tonawanda), a subsidiary of Fortistar LLC. In September 2021, Digihost and North
         Tonawanda executed a Pre-Closing Improvements Work Authorization and Indemnity
         Agreement permitting Digihost to make pre-closing improvements at the Facility,
         including the construction of a datacenter to accommodate cryptocurrency mining. After

Document Accession #: 20260803-3037           Filed Date: 08/03/2026

         Docket No. IN25-4-000                                                                    -2-

         certain regulatory approvals were obtained,1 in February 2023, Digihost consummated
         the acquisition of FNT and thus the Facility.

         4.    On February 17, 2022, prior to its acquisition of FNT, Digihost interconnected a
         cryptocurrency load to the Facility that it constructed pursuant to the Pre-Closing
         Improvements Work Authorization and Indemnity Agreement.

         5.     Though Digihost had initiated discussions with NYISO regarding the power
         source as of January 31, 2022, Digihost did not submit an interconnection proposal to
         NYISO either before or during the Relevant Period in which Digihost interconnected its
         cryptocurrency load to the Facility.

         6.     On April 21, 2022, Digihost President Alec Amar received a letter from National
         Grid stating that the increased demand at the Facility raised concerns with reliability,
         noting that the demand was not preceded by adequate notice and appropriate analysis,
         and advising Digihost to reduce its demand at the Facility or risk National Grid tripping
         Digihost’s load. Digihost received a second warning letter from National Grid on April
         29, 2022.

         7.    Digihost’s on-site load at the Facility fluctuated during the Relevant Period and
         peaked at approximately 30 MW before Digihost dropped its load entirely on April 30,
         2022.

         8.     In September 2022, Digihost submitted an interconnection request to NYISO for a
         System Impact Study, which was necessary for approval of Digihost’s cryptocurrency
         load at the Facility. The Facility has since been accepted as a behind meter resource by
         NYISO. In December 2025, the NYISO Operating Committee approved the System
         Impact Study Report for the cryptocurrency load without system modifications.

         9.   Enforcement opened this investigation following a July 8, 2024 referral from
         Potomac Economics, Ltd., NYISO’s Market Monitoring Unit.

         II.    Violation

         10.   Enforcement determined that Digihost violated NYISO Tariff Section 3.9.1.
         During the Relevant Period, NYISO Tariff Section 3.9.1 stated:

                Any Eligible Customer proposing to interconnect its Load or Large Facility
                with the NYS Power System shall submit its interconnection proposal to

                1 See, e.g., Fortistar North Tonawanda LLC, 181 FERC ¶ 61,224 (2022)
         (declaratory ruling and approval of the transfer of ownership interests underlying the
         section 203 transaction).

Document Accession #: 20260803-3037            Filed Date: 08/03/2026

         Docket No. IN25-4-000                                                                   -3-

                the ISO. The ISO, in cooperation with the Transmission Owner with whose
                system the Eligible Customer proposes to interconnect, shall perform
                technical studies to determine whether the proposed interconnection may
                degrade system reliability or adversely affect the operation of the NYS
                Power System. The technical studies shall be conducted in accordance with
                the procedures specified in Section 3.9.2. The proposed interconnection
                shall not proceed if the ISO concludes in the study that the proposed
                interconnection may degrade system reliability or adversely affect the
                operation of the NYS Power System. If the proposal is rejected, the ISO
                shall provide in writing the reasons why the proposal was rejected.

         11.    Enforcement determined that Digihost violated this section during the Relevant
         Period when it interconnected its cryptocurrency load to the Facility without submitting
         an interconnection proposal to the ISO. Digihost did not submit an interconnection
         proposal prior to or at any time during the Relevant Period.

         III.   Stipulation and Consent Agreement

         12.    Enforcement and Digihost have resolved the Investigation by means of the
         attached Agreement.

         13.   Digihost stipulates to the facts set forth in Section II of the Agreement, but neither
         admits nor denies the violation described in Section III of the Agreement.

         14.    Digihost agrees to pay a civil penalty of $45,000 to the United States Treasury.

         15.    Digihost agrees to submit an annual compliance monitoring report to Enforcement
         for two years with a third year at Enforcement’s discretion.

         IV.    Determination of Appropriate Remedies and Sanctions

         16.    In recommending the appropriate remedy, Enforcement considered the factors
         described in the Revised Policy Statement on Penalty Guidelines,2 including the
         involvement of high-level personnel in the violation.3


                2Enforcement of Statutes, Orders, Rules, and Regulations, Revised Policy
         Statement on Penalty Guidelines, 132 FERC ¶ 61,216 (2010).
                3  The following is applicable to small entities including businesses with 1,500 or
         fewer employees, independent schools / universities, trade associations, other non-profits,
         cities, counties, towns, townships, villages, school districts, and other special districts -
         The National Ombudsman resolves concerns of uneven or excessive federal regulatory
         enforcement. Reviews are confidential and do not waive the right to pursue

Document Accession #: 20260803-3037            Filed Date: 08/03/2026

         Docket No. IN25-4-000                                                                    -4-

         17.    The Commission concludes that the Agreement is a fair and equitable resolution of
         the matters concerned and is in the public interest, as it reflects the nature and seriousness
         of the conduct and recognizes the specific considerations stated above and in the
         Agreement.

         18.   The Commission also concludes that Digihost’s civil penalty is consistent with the
         Revised Policy Statement on Penalty Guidelines.4

         19.   The Commission directs Digihost to make the civil penalty payment as required by
         the Agreement within ten days after the Effective Date of the Agreement.

         The Commission orders:

               The attached Stipulation and Consent Agreement is hereby approved without
         modification.

         By the Commission.

         (SEAL)




                                                          Carlos D. Clay,
                                                         Deputy Secretary.




         administrative appeals or any other legal action. 888-REG-FAIR /

         Digi Power X Inc.


                            STIPULATION AND CONSENT AGREEMENT

         I.     INTRODUCTION

         1.     The Office of Enforcement and Regulatory Accounting (Enforcement) of the
         Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (Commission) and Digi Power X Inc. f/k/a
         Digihost Technology Inc. (Digihost) enter into this Stipulation and Consent Agreement
         (Agreement) to resolve a nonpublic, formal investigation (the Investigation) conducted
         by Enforcement pursuant to Part 1b of the Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R. Part 1b
         (2025). The Investigation examined whether Digihost violated the New York
         Independent Systems Operator (NYISO) Open Access Transmission Tariff (Tariff)
         Section 3.9.1 from February 17, 2022 to April 30, 2022 (Relevant Period) when Digihost
         interconnected its cryptocurrency load to the Fortistar North Tonawanda LLC (FNT) co-
         generation facility (Facility) without first submitting the required interconnection
         proposal to NYISO.

         2.     Digihost stipulates to the facts in Section II, but neither admits nor denies the
         alleged violation in Section III. Digihost agrees to: (a) pay a civil penalty of $45,000 to
         the United States Treasury; and (b) be subject to compliance monitoring as provided
         more fully below.

         II.    STIPULATIONS

         Enforcement and Digihost hereby stipulate and agree to the following facts.

         3.     FNT owned and operated a 55 MW co-generation facility located in North
         Tonawanda, New York that is interconnected to the 115kV transmission system of
         Niagara Mohawk Power Corporation d/b/a National Grid. In March 2021, Digihost
         signed an agreement to purchase FNT from North Tonawanda Holdings, LLC (North
         Tonawanda), a subsidiary of Fortistar LLC. In September 2021, Digihost and North
         Tonawanda executed a Pre-Closing Improvements Work Authorization and Indemnity
         Agreement permitting Digihost to make pre-closing improvements at the Facility,
         including the construction of a datacenter to accommodate cryptocurrency mining. After

         certain regulatory approvals were obtained,1 in February 2023, Digihost consummated
         the acquisition of FNT and thus the Facility.

         4.    On February 17, 2022, prior to its acquisition of FNT, Digihost interconnected a
         cryptocurrency load to the Facility that it constructed pursuant to the Pre-Closing
         Improvements Work Authorization and Indemnity Agreement.

         5.    Though Digihost had initiated discussions with NYISO regarding the power
         source as of January 31, 2022, Digihost did not submit an interconnection proposal to
         NYISO either before or during the Relevant Period in which Digihost interconnected its
         cryptocurrency load to the Facility.

         6.     On April 21, 2022, Digihost President Alec Amar received a letter from National
         Grid stating that the increased demand at the Facility raised concerns with reliability,
         noting that the demand was not preceded by adequate notice and appropriate analysis,
         and advising Digihost to reduce its demand at the Facility or risk National Grid tripping
         Digihost’s load. Digihost received a second warning letter from National Grid on April
         29, 2022

         7.    Digihost’s on-site load at the Facility fluctuated during the Relevant Period and
         peaked at approximately 30 MW before Digihost dropped its load entirely on April 30,

         8.     In September 2022, Digihost submitted an interconnection request to NYISO for a
         System Impact Study, which was necessary for approval of Digihost’s cryptocurrency
         load at the Facility. The Facility has since been accepted as a behind meter resource by

         9.   Enforcement opened this investigation following a July 8, 2024 referral from
         Potomac Economics, Ltd., NYISO’s Market Monitoring Unit.

         III.   VIOLATION

         10.    During the Relevant Period, NYISO Tariff Section 3.9.1 stated:

                       Any Eligible Customer proposing to interconnect its Load or Large Facility
                       with the NYS Power System shall submit its interconnection proposal to
                       the ISO. The ISO, in cooperation with the Transmission Owner with whose
                       system the Eligible Customer proposes to interconnect, shall perform

         1 See, e.g., Fortistar North Tonawanda LLC, 181 FERC ¶ 61,224 (2022) (declaratory

         ruling and approval of the transfer of ownership interests underlying the section 203
         transaction).

                                                     2

Document Accession #: 20260803-3037            Filed Date: 08/03/2026



                       technical studies to determine whether the proposed interconnection may
                       degrade system reliability or adversely affect the operation of the NYS
                       Power System. The technical studies shall be conducted in accordance with
                       the procedures specified in Section 3.9.2. The proposed interconnection
                       shall not proceed if the ISO concludes in the study that the proposed
                       interconnection may degrade system reliability or adversely affect the
                       operation of the NYS Power System. If the proposal is rejected, the ISO
                       shall provide in writing the reasons why the proposal was rejected.

         11.    Enforcement determined that Digihost violated this section during the Relevant
         Period when it interconnected its cryptocurrency load to the Facility without submitting
         an interconnection proposal to the ISO. Digihost did not submit an interconnection
         proposal prior to or at any time during the Relevant Period.

         IV.    REMEDIES AND SANCTIONS

         12.    For purposes of settling the claims released pursuant to Paragraph 19, Digihost
         agrees with the facts as stipulated in Section II of this Agreement, but it neither admits
         nor denies the violation described in Section III of this Agreement. Digihost further
         agrees to undertake obligations set forth in the following paragraphs.

                A.     Civil Penalty

         13.     Digihost agrees to pay a civil penalty of $45,000 to the United States Treasury, by
         wire transfer, within ten days after the Effective Date of this Agreement, as defined
         herein.

                B.     Compliance

         14.    Digihost shall make annual compliance monitoring reports to Enforcement for two
         years following the Effective Date of this Agreement. The first annual compliance
         monitoring report shall be submitted no later than 30 days after the end of the one-year
         reporting period that follows the Effective Date of this Agreement. The second annual
         compliance monitoring report shall be submitted one year from the date of the first
         report. After receipt of the second annual report, Enforcement may, at its sole discretion,
         require Digihost to submit a report for one additional year.

         15.     Each compliance monitoring report shall: (1) identify any known violations of
         Commission regulations or the Tariff that occurred during the applicable period,
         including a description of the nature of the violation and what steps were taken to rectify
         the situation; (2) describe all compliance measures and procedures Digihost instituted or
         modified during the reporting period related to compliance with Commission regulations
         or the Tariff; and (3) describe all Tariff- or Commission-related compliance training(s)
         that Digihost administered during the reporting period, including the dates such
                                                       3

Document Accession #: 20260803-3037            Filed Date: 08/03/2026



         training(s) occurred, the topics covered, and the procedures used to confirm which
         personnel attended.

         16.    Each compliance monitoring report shall also include an affidavit executed by an
         officer of Digihost stating that the report is true and accurate to the best of his/her
         knowledge.

         17.  Upon request by Enforcement, Digihost shall provide to Enforcement
         documentation supporting the contents of its reports.

         V.     TERMS

         18. The “Effective Date” of this Agreement shall be the date on which the
         Commission issues an order approving this Agreement without material modification.

         19.     Commission approval of this Agreement without material modification shall
         release Digihost and forever bar the Commission from holding Digihost, any affiliated
         entity, any successor in interest, and their respective agents, officers, directors, or
         employees, both past and present, liable for any and all administrative or civil claims
         brought by the Commission arising out of Enforcement’s determination of the specific
         violation addressed in this Agreement that arose during the Relevant Period.

         20.    Failure by Digihost to make the civil penalty payment or to comply with the
         compliance obligations agreed to herein, or any other provision of this Agreement, shall
         be deemed a violation of a final order of the Commission issued pursuant to the Federal
         Power Act (FPA), 16 U.S.C. §792, et seq., and may subject Digihost to additional action
         under the enforcement provisions of the FPA.

         21.    If Digihost does not make the required civil penalty payment described above
         within the time agreed by the parties, interest will be calculated pursuant to 18 C.F.R. §
         35.19a(a)(2)(iii) from the date that payment is due, in addition to the penalty specified
         above and any other enforcement action and penalty that the Commission may take or
         impose.

         22.     This Agreement binds Digihost and its agents, successors, and assignees. This
         Agreement does not create any additional or independent obligations on Digihost, or any
         affiliated entity, its agents, officers, directors, or employees, other than the obligations
         identified in this Agreement.

         23.    The signatories to this Agreement agree that they enter into the Agreement
         voluntarily and that, other than the recitations set forth herein, no tender, offer or promise
         of any kind by any member, employee, officer, director, agent or representative of
         Enforcement or Digihost has been made to induce the signatories or any other party to
         enter into the Agreement.
                                                       4

Document Accession #: 20260803-3037           Filed Date: 08/03/2026




         24.    Unless the Commission issues an order approving the Agreement in its entirety
         and without material modification, the Agreement shall be null and void and of no effect
         whatsoever, and neither Enforcement nor Digihost shall be bound by any provision or
         term of the Agreement, unless otherwise agreed to in writing by Enforcement and
         Digihost.

         25.    In connection with the civil penalty provided for herein, Digihost agrees that the
         Commission’s order approving the Agreement without material modification shall be a
         final and unappealable order assessing a civil penalty under section 316A(b) of the FPA,
         16 U.S.C. § 825o-1(b). Digihost waives findings of fact and conclusions of law,
         rehearing of any Commission order approving the Agreement without material
         modification, and judicial review by any court of any Commission order approving the
         Agreement without material modification.

         26.   This Agreement can be modified only if in writing and signed by Enforcement and
         Digihost, and any modifications will not be effective unless approved by the
         Commission.

         27.    Each of the undersigned warrants that he or she is an authorized representative of
         the entity designated, is authorized to bind such entity, and accepts the Agreement on the
         entity’s behalf.

         28.    The undersigned representative of Digihost affirms that he or she has read the
         Agreement, that all of the matters set forth in the Agreement are true and correct to the
         best of his or her knowledge, information and belief, and that he or she understands that
         the Agreement is entered into by Enforcement in express reliance on those
         representations.

         29.  This Agreement is executed in duplicate, each of which so executed shall be
         deemed to be an original.

Document Accession #: 20260417-3061            Filed Date: 04/17/2026




                                      195 FERC ¶ 61,048
                                  UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                           FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION


         Before Commissioners: Laura V. Swett, Chairman;
                               David Rosner, Lindsay S. See,
                               Judy W. Chang, and David LaCerte.


         Interstate Power and Light Company                                  Docket No. IN25-6-000


                 ORDER APPROVING STIPULATION AND CONSENT AGREEMENT


                                           (Issued April 17, 2026)

         1.     The Commission approves the attached Stipulation and Consent Agreement
         (Agreement) between the Office of Enforcement and Regulatory Accounting
         (Enforcement) and Interstate Power and Light Company (Interstate). This order is in the
         public interest because the Agreement resolves on fair and equitable terms Enforcement’s
         investigation (Investigation) under Part 1b of the Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R.
         Part 1b (2025), into whether Alliant Energy Corporate Services, Inc. (AECS), acting on
         the behalf of Interstate, misrepresented to Potomac Economics (Potomac), the market
         monitor for the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (MISO), the operational
         status of the Marshalltown Combustion Turbine generating station (MTown CT) in
         connection with a routine audit performed by Potomac in December 2023 and January
         2024 (the Relevant Period).

         2.     Interstate stipulates to the facts in Section II of the Agreement but it neither admits
         nor denies the alleged violations described in Section III of the Agreement. Interstate
         agrees to: (a) pay a civil penalty of $70,000 to the United States Treasury; and (b) be
         subject to compliance monitoring as provided more fully below.

Document Accession #: 20260417-3061             Filed Date: 04/17/2026

         Docket No. IN25-6-000                                                                  -2-

         I.     Facts

         3.   The MTown CT1 is a three-unit natural gas fired combustion turbine that
         commenced operations in 1978. Each combustion turbine unit has a capacity rating of
         63 MW. MTown CT is owned and operated by Interstate.2

         4.    AECS is responsible for bidding each of the MTown CT Units into MISO’s
         annual Planning Resource Auction (PRA). This includes MISO’s 2023-24 PRA, which
         occurred on April 21, 2023.

         5.     MISO’s 2023-24 PRA was the first to implement MISO’s seasonal market design.
         Under this construct, resources like MTown CT were bid based on their seasonal
         availability and resources that clear the PRA are, in turn, subject to seasonal performance
         requirements.3 Where resources are unable to meet those requirements due to prolonged
         outages they are generally required to procure replacement capacity or pay Capacity
         Replacement Non-Compliance Charges (CRNCC Charges).4 MISO’s Tariff imposes
         CRNCC Charges on capacity resources whose outages “were not planned but were
         known or could have been reasonably anticipated at the time of the PRA . . . .”5




                1
                 The Marshalltown combustion turbine generating station is distinct from the
         three-unit natural gas fired combined cycle Marshalltown Generating Station that
         commenced operations in 2017 and three-unit Sutherland Generating Station that retired
         in 2010 and 2016. In order to avoid confusion, the Marshalltown combustion turbine
         generating station is referred to in this settlement as MTown CT, which is consistent with
         the resource’s naming convention with the MISO.
                2
                Interstate and AECS are both wholly owned subsidiaries of Alliant Energy
         Corporation, for which AECS is the centralized service company.
                3
                   See MISO, FERC Electric Tariff, Module E-1, § 69A.4.1 (37.0) (establishing
         criteria for the Seasonal Accredited Capacity of Capacity Resources) and § 69A.7.1
         (49.0.0) (discussing procedures for the PRA, including those concerning the participation
         of Seasonal Accredited Capacity resources); see also id., Module A, § 1.S (74.0.0)
         (defining Seasonal Accredited Capacity as “The amount of accredited Capacity, for a
         given Season, in MW, assigned to a Planning Resource after accounting for its historic
         availability.”).
                4
                    Id., Module E-1, § 69A.3.1.h(a) (40.0.0).
                5
                    Id.

Document Accession #: 20260417-3061            Filed Date: 04/17/2026

         Docket No. IN25-6-000                                                                   -3-

         6.      In the Summer and Fall seasons of the 2023–24 PRA, AECS offered in the full
         capacity of MTown CT Unit 1 (one of the three combustion turbine units operating at
         Marshalltown). When those seasons came to pass, however, MTown CT Unit 1 was only
         partially available due to derates caused by equipment failures.

         7.     On December 12, 2023, Potomac e-mailed AECS indicating that Potomac was
         conducting an “audit” of “outages associated” with MTown CT Unit 1 (the Audit
         Inquiry). Specifically, Potomac sought information concerning a forced outage ticket for
         MTown CT Unit 1 that was dated in December 2022. The Audit Inquiry indicated that
         Potomac was looking for information concerning the underlying “equipment failure” and
         any “plans for repair” to the unit.

         8.     The Audit Inquiry further stated that Potomac was acting in its capacity as MISO’s
         Independent Market Monitor and contained in the body of the email the text of Section
         35.41(b) of the Commission’s regulations, which prohibits anyone authorized under the
         Federal Power Act to make sales for resale of electric energy, capacity, or ancillary
         services at market-based rates to make a false or misleading statement to, among others,
         Commission-approved market monitors, such as Potomac.

         9.      After the Audit Inquiry was received, AECS employees began preparing a
         response. Contemporaneous communications indicate that those employees were aware
         of the relationship between Potomac’s inquiry into the prolonged derate at Marshalltown
         Unit 1 and the possibility of CRNCC Charges.

         10.    On December 20, 2023, AECS employees provided their response to the Audit
         Inquiry (the Audit Response). In the Audit Response, AECS made specific factual
         representations concerning MTown CT Unit 1 and the circumstances around its return to
         service.

         11.     AECS explained in the Audit Response how the December 2022 forced outage
         ticket that was the subject of the Audit Inquiry was linked to an earlier forced outage at
         MTown CT Unit 1 that occurred in August 2022.

         12.    AECS also stated in the Audit Response that, between August 2022 and May
         2023, AECS had taken steps to identify a vendor to perform repairs on MTown CT Unit
         1 and during that period had vetted a vendor that could provide those services.

         13.   AECS represented to Potomac that at some point between May 2023 and
         September 2023, a new forced outage occurred at MTown CT Unit 3 (another of the three
         combustion turbine units operating at Marshalltown).

Document Accession #: 20260417-3061           Filed Date: 04/17/2026

         Docket No. IN25-6-000                                                                 -4-

         14.    AECS also explained in the Audit Response that AECS decided to prioritize
         repairs to MTown CT Unit 3 using the vendor that had been vetted to repair MTown CT
         Unit 1, which could only repair one turbine at a time.

         15.    AECS went on to describe in the Audit Response how the decision to prioritize
         repairs to MTown CT Unit 3, and other issues, delayed MTown CT Unit 1’s return to
         service.

         16.   On December 20, 2023, AECS sent the Audit Response to Potomac. The AECS
         employee who prepared the Audit Response provided a copy of the response to a
         supervisor but did not obtain supervisory review of its contents.

         17.   On December 27, 2023, Potomac provided AECS a series of follow-up questions
         concerning the Audit Response.

         18.     On January 10, 2024, AECS provided Potomac with a new timeline and
         description of events (the Revised Response), which both revealed and corrected several
         false statements in the Audit Response.

         19.   Although AECS’s Audit Response indicated MTown CT Unit 3 had suffered a
         new outage in or later than May 2023, in the Revised Response AECS explained that in
         fact MTown CT Unit 3 had been significantly derated since July 2022.

         20.    In its Revised Response, AECS explained that it had sent damaged components
         for MTown CT Unit 3 to a vendor for repairs in November 2022. In September 2023, the
         vendor released MTown CT Unit 3 back to AECS and AECS placed it into service. That
         same month AECS began the process of securing funding and attempted to vet an
         alternative vendor for MTown CT Unit 1 but subsequently determined to replace MTown
         CT Unit 1 in November 2023. AECS secured funding and purchased a new unit in
         November 2023.

         21.    The representations AECS made in the Audit Response were generally consistent
         with a timeline that would reduce the likelihood of the imposition of CRNCC Charges
         because they suggested a May 2023 (or later) outage at MTown CT Unit 3 contributed to
         a delay in MTown CT Unit 1’s return to service. However, in light of AECS’s
         corrections in the Revised Response, Potomac went on to recommend CRNCC Charges
         be assessed against Interstate arising from the availability status of MTown CT Unit 1
         during the Summer 2023 and Fall 2023 seasons. Those charges subsequently were
         assessed against, and paid by, Interstate.

         22.     The AECS employee who prepared and submitted the Audit Response to Potomac
         on behalf of Interstate failed to exercise sufficient care in preparing the Audit Response;
         failed to make use of data sources available to them to confirm the accuracy of the Audit

Document Accession #: 20260417-3061            Filed Date: 04/17/2026

         Docket No. IN25-6-000                                                                   -5-

         Response; and failed to secure supervisory review to help support the accuracy of the Audit
         Response. AECS asserts that this evidence establishes that the inaccurate statements
         contained in the Audit Response were made inadvertently.

         23.   AECS, on its own behalf and on behalf of Interstate, fully cooperated with
         Enforcement during the Investigation.

         II.    Violations

         24.   Enforcement concluded that Interstate, by submitting false information to Potomac
         through AECS, violated 18 C.F.R. § 35.41(b)’s requirement that Sellers “must . . . not
         submit false or misleading information . . . in any communication with . . . Commission
         approved market monitors[.]”6

                           STIPULATION AND CONSENT AGREEMENT


         I.    INTRODUCTION

        1.     The Office of Enforcement and Regulatory Accounting (Enforcement) of the
        Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (Commission) and Interstate Power and Light
        Company (Interstate), enter into this Stipulation and Consent Agreement (Agreement) to
        resolve a nonpublic, preliminary investigation (the Investigation) conducted by
        Enforcement pursuant to Part 1b of the Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R. Part 1b
        (2025). As described more fully in Section II below, the Investigation concerned whether
        Alliant Energy Corporate Services, Inc. (AECS), acting on behalf of Interstate,
        misrepresented to Potomac Economics (Potomac), the market monitor for the
        Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (MISO), the operational status of the
        Marshalltown Combustion Turbine generating station (MTown CT)1 in connection with a
        routine audit performed by Potomac in December 2023 and January 2024 (the Relevant
        Period).

        2.     Interstate stipulates to the facts in Section II, but neither admits nor denies the
        alleged violations in Section III. Interstate agrees to: (a) pay a civil penalty of $70,000 to
        the United States Treasury; and (b) be subject to compliance monitoring as provided more
        fully below.

         II.   STIPULATIONS

         3.    Enforcement and Interstate hereby stipulate and agree to the following facts.


         1
           The Marshalltown Combustion Turbine generating station is distinct from the three-unit
         natural gas fired combined cycle Marshalltown Generating Station that commenced
         operations in 2017 and the three-unit Sutherland Generating Station that retired in 2010
         and 2016. In order to avoid confusion, the Marshalltown Combustion Turbine generating
         station is referred to in this settlement as MTown CT, which is consistent with the
         resource’s naming convention with MISO.

         4.     MTown CT is a three-unit natural gas fired combustion turbine that commenced
         operations in 1978. Each combustion turbine unit has a capacity rating of 63 MW.
         MTown CT is owned and operated by Interstate.2

         5.    AECS is responsible for bidding each of the MTown CT Units into MISO’s
         annual Planning Resource Auction (PRA). This includes MISO’s 2023-24 PRA, which
         occurred on April 21, 2023.

         6.     MISO’s 2023-24 PRA was the first to implement MISO’s seasonal market design.
         Under this construct, resources like MTown CT are bid based on their seasonal availability
         and resources that clear the PRA are, in turn, subject to seasonal performance
         requirements.3 Where resources are unable to meet those requirements due to prolonged
         outages, they are generally required to procure replacement capacity or pay Capacity
         Replacement Non-Compliance Charges (CRNCC Charges).4 MISO’s Tariff imposes
         CRNCC Charges on capacity resources whose outages “were not planned but were known
         or could have been reasonably anticipated at the time of the PRA . . . .”5

         7.      In the Summer and Fall seasons of the 2023–24 PRA, AECS offered in the full
         capacity of MTown CT Unit 1 (one of the three combustion turbine units operating at
         Marshalltown). When those seasons came to pass, however, MTown CT Unit 1 was only
         partially available due to derates caused by equipment failures.

         8.     On December 12, 2023, Potomac e-mailed AECS indicating that Potomac was
         conducting an “audit” of “outages associated” with MTown CT Unit 1 (the Audit Inquiry).
         Specifically, Potomac sought information concerning a forced outage ticket for MTown CT
         Unit 1 that was dated in December 2022. The Audit Inquiry indicated that Potomac was

         15.   AECS also explained in the Audit Response that AECS decided to prioritize repairs

         17.    On December 20, 2023, AECS sent the Audit Response to Potomac. The AECS

         18.   On December 27, 2023, Potomac provided AECS a series of follow-up questions

         19.   On January 10, 2024, AECS provided Potomac with a new timeline and description

         20.   Although AECS’s Audit Response indicated MTown CT Unit 3 had suffered a new

         MTown CT Unit 3 had been significantly derated since July 2022.

         21.    In its Revised Response, AECS explained that it had sent damaged components for

                                      195 FERC ¶ 61,019
                                 UNITED STATES OF AMERICA

         Before Commissioners: Laura V. Swett, Chairman;

                               Judy W. Chang, and David LaCerte.

         MPH Rockaway Peakers, LLC and                                 Docket No. IN25-10-000

                    ORDER APPROVING STIPULATION AND CONSENT AGREEMENT

                                           (Issued April 8, 2026)

                The Commission approves the attached Stipulation and Consent Agreement
         (Agreement) between the Office of Enforcement and Regulatory Accounting
         (Enforcement) and MPH Rockaway Peakers, LLC (MPH-Rockaway), and Bayswater
         Peaking Facility, LLC (Bayswater) (collectively, Rockaway). This order is in the public
         interest because the Agreement resolves on fair and equitable terms Enforcement’s
         investigation (Investigation) under Part 1b of the Commission’s regulations,
         18 C.F.R. Part 1b (2025).

                The Investigation examined whether Rockaway violated the New York
         Independent System Operator, Inc.’s (NYISO) Market Administration and Control Area
         Services Tariff (Tariff) and Commission regulations when it, (a) conducted summer
         capability tests in configurations that differ from expected operations; (b) did not inform
         NYISO of derates; (c) submitted inaccurate Generating Availability Data System
         (GADS) data1; and (d) oversold capacity and reserves from its Far Rockaway GT1
         peaking unit (GT1).

                Rockaway stipulates to the facts in Section II of the Agreement and admits the
         violations in Section III of the Agreement. Rockaway agrees to pay sanctions and civil

                1
                  GADS is a mandatory industry program used by the North American Electric
         Reliability Corporation (NERC) to collect information about the performance, reliability,
         and availability of generating units. GADS reporting, which is mandatory for certain
         NERC-registered entities, requires submitting specific GADS codes that provide the
         reason a resource is derated or on outage. NYISO uses GADS reports to determine a
         generator’s capacity value based on its outages in earlier periods.

         Docket No. IN25-10-000                                                                  -2-


         penalties of $185,000 and disgorge $626,642 in capacity and reserve market
         overpayments. Rockaway has already disgorged $299,298 and paid tariff-based2
         sanctions of $149,649 to NYISO. Therefore, Rockaway will (a) pay a civil penalty of
         $35,351 to the United States Treasury, which takes into consideration credit for the
         NYISO sanctions it has already paid, (b) disgorge a balance of $327,344 plus interest to
         NYISO; and (c) be subject to compliance monitoring as provided more fully below.

         I.     FACTS

                 Bayswater owns GT1, which is an approximately 60.5 MW natural gas-fired
         electric generation facility. Bayswater is a wholly owned indirect subsidiary of
         MPH-Rockaway, which is owned by funds managed and controlled by Hull Street
         Energy, LLC. The Commission authorized Bayswater and MPH-Rockaway to sell
         energy, capacity, and ancillary services at market-based rates.3 Bayswater sells all of its
         output to MPH-Rockaway, which in turn resells it into the NYISO markets.
         MPH-Rockaway is the NYISO Market Participant for Bayswater and GT1.

               MPH-Rockaway also indirectly owns Jamaica Bay Peaking Facility, LLC
         (Jamaica Bay), which owns and operates Far Rockaway GT2 (GT2), an approximately
         60.5 MW electric generation facility that is co-located with GT1. MPH-Rockaway
         purchases from Jamaica Bay the output of GT2 and resells it into the NYISO markets.
         MPH-Rockaway is the NYISO Market Participant for Jamaica Bay and GT2.

                GT1 and GT2 share certain equipment and, in July 2021, GT2 was modified to
         have dual fuel capabilities so that it could also run on natural gas. When both units run
         on natural gas at the same time, GT2’s gas compressor becomes part of GT1’s auxiliary
         load. As a result, when both units are run simultaneously on gas, GT1’s auxiliary load
         increases by approximately 2.7 MW and its energy output decreases by that amount.

                Tariff section 5.12.1.2 requires all Installed Capacity (ICAP) Suppliers, such as
         GT1, to perform Dependable Maximum Net Capability (DMNC) tests. Pursuant to Tariff
         section 2.4, the DMNC is defined as a measure of “[t]he sustained maximum net output
         of a Generator, or, where appropriate, an Aggregation, as demonstrated by the
         performance of a test or through actual operation, averaged over a continuous time period


                2
                  NYISO Tariff section 5.12.12.2 permits NYISO to impose sanctions and
         penalties for certain capacity market violations.
                3
               Bayswater Peaking Facility, LLC, Docket No. ER02-669-000 (Feb. 27, 2002);
         MPH-Rockaway Peakers, LLC, Docket No. ER20-2060-000 (Aug. 13, 2020).

Document Accession #: 20260408-3063           Filed Date: 04/08/2026

         Docket No. IN25-10-000                                                                -3-


         as defined in the ISO Procedures.” The procedures for establishing the DMNC are
         outlined in section 4.2 of the Installed Capacity Manual (ICAP Manual) and require
         DMNC confirmation each year to be conducted in a way that reflects the expected
         operating configuration and fuel that will be used at peak summer and winter load
         conditions.

                Since mid-July 2021, GT1 and GT2 have frequently been fired together on gas
         during summer peak conditions, which resulted in an effective 2.7 MW derate for GT1 on
         those occasions. However, the derate was not reflected in GT1’s ICAP for summer 2021
         because that ICAP was established in September 2020 based on DMNC data established
         with the two generators running separately.

                Rockaway continued to follow the same erroneous DMNC data submission
         practice for the summer 2022 and summer 2023 capacity seasons, which resulted in the
         same 2.7 MW over-estimation of the GT1 ICAP value and violated protocols for setting
         the DMNC as set forth in the ICAP Manual.

                Tariff section 5.12.7 requires ICAP Suppliers to “notify the ISO of any outages,”
         and Rockaway should have, but did not, notify NYISO in its Outage Scheduler System of
         the 2.7 MW derate starting July 2021 as well as certain other mechanical and ambient
         outages that occurred from January 2021 until March 2023. Nor did Rockaway
         consistently and accurately submit GADS reports reflecting GT1’s reduced capability as
         required by Tariff section 5.12.5.1 during the same period.

                Rockaway’s noncompliance with Tariff section 5.12.5.1 had a downstream effect
