cards.body:
Document Accession #: 20260407-3069           Filed Date: 04/07/2026




                                      195 FERC ¶ 61,016
                                 UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                          FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

         Before Commissioners: Laura V. Swett, Chairman;
                               David Rosner, Lindsay S. See,
                               Judy W. Chang, and David LaCerte.

         Terra-Gen, LLC                                                    Docket No. IN26-2-000

                ORDER APPROVING STIPULATION AND CONSENT AGREEMENT

                                           (Issued April 7, 2026)

                The Commission approves the attached Stipulation and Consent Agreement
         (Agreement) between the Office of Enforcement and Regulatory Accounting
         (Enforcement) and Terra-Gen, LLC (Terra-Gen). This order is in the public interest
         because the Agreement resolves on fair and equitable terms Enforcement’s investigation
         (Investigation) under Part 1b of the Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R. Part 1b (2025),
         into whether: (a) Terra-Gen’s participation in the California Independent System
         Operator (CAISO) ancillary services market during the period of July 7, 2020 through
         April 17, 2022 (Relevant Period) violated the CAISO Open Access Transmission Tariff
         (Tariff), the Commission’s Market Behavior Rule (18 C.F.R. § 35.41(a)), section 222 of
         the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. § 824v), and the Commission’s Anti-Manipulation
         Rule (18 C.F.R. § 1.c.2); and (b) Terra-Gen violated the Commission’s Duty of Candor
         Rule (18 C.F.R. § 35.41(b)) in connection with a compliance report that it submitted to
         Enforcement pursuant to a prior Commission-approved settlement of an unrelated matter.

                Terra-Gen stipulates to the facts set forth in Section II of the Agreement and
         admits the violations set forth in Section III.A of the Agreement. Terra-Gen neither
         admits nor denies the alleged violation set forth in Section III.B of the Agreement.
         Terra-Gen agrees to: (a) pay a civil penalty of $4,950,000 to the United States Treasury;
         (b) disgorge $681,007, plus interest, to CAISO; and (c) be subject to the compliance
         monitoring requirements as provided in the Agreement.

         I.    Facts

               A.      Background

                Terra-Gen is a Delaware limited liability company. Through subsidiaries, Terra-
         Gen owns and operates multiple resources in the CAISO footprint, including the
         resources at issue in the Agreement: Mojave 89 and Mojave 90 (together, Resources).

Document Accession #: 20260407-3069                Filed Date: 04/07/2026

         Docket No. IN26-2-000                                                               -2-

         4.     Mojave 16/17/18 LLC (a wholly-owned subsidiary of Terra-Gen) owns and
         operates Mojave 89. Mojave 16/17/18 LLC has market-based rate authorization from the
         Commission.1

         5.     Mojave 3/4/5 LLC (another wholly-owned subsidiary of Terra-Gen) owns and
         operates Mojave 90. Mojave 3/4/5 LLC also has market-based rate authorization from
         the Commission.2

         6.     During the Relevant Period, TGP Energy Management, LLC (TGP Energy) was
         the Scheduling Coordinator for both Resources. TGP Energy is another wholly-owned
         subsidiary of Terra-Gen.

         7.     At the beginning of the Relevant Period, each Resource consisted of a wind farm
         and an associated battery energy storage system (BESS) with a single CAISO resource
         ID, because each Resource was registered as a hybrid resource. However, on November
         19, 2020, Terra-Gen converted the Mojave 90 registration from hybrid to co-located.
         This conversion resulted in two separate CAISO resource IDs for Mojave 90—one ID for
         the wind component and one ID for the BESS component. Mojave 89 underwent a
         similar conversion after the Relevant Period.

                   B.       Terra-Gen’s participation in the CAISO ancillary services market

         8.     During the Relevant Period, Terra-Gen (through TGP Energy): (a) offered the
         Resources into the CAISO day-ahead market to provide ancillary services; and (b)
         obtained ancillary service awards based on those offers. Under the CAISO Tariff, these
         awards were binding in the real-time market and required Terra-Gen (acting through TGP
         Energy) to place the Resources on automatic generation control for the duration of the
         awards, so that CAISO could directly dispatch the Resources when and as needed.3

         9.     However, in numerous hours during the Relevant Period, when the Resources
         received binding regulation-down awards from CAISO (i.e. when CAISO instructed the
         Resources to purchase energy off the grid and store it in the Resources’ BESSs) and the
         real-time Locational Marginal Price (LMP) was high, Terra-Gen (through its relevant
         subsidiaries) employed a strategy to avoid this obligation by:

                   a.       Claiming outages for the Resources’ BESS, even though there was no
                            legitimate basis for doing so; and/or


                   1
                       Mojave 16/17/18 LLC, Docket No. ER19-1662-000 (May 30, 2019) (delegated
         order).
                   2
                       Mojave 3/4/5 LLC, Docket No. ER19-1660-000 (May 30, 2019) (delegated
         order).
                   3
                       See generally CAISO Tariff sections 8.7, 34.13, and 37.3.1.1.

Document Accession #: 20260407-3069           Filed Date: 04/07/2026

         Docket No. IN26-2-000                                                               -3-

                b.     Removing the Resources from automatic generation control, and therefore
                       preventing CAISO from implementing regulation-down awards, even
                       though the Resources were operationally capable of meeting regulation-
                       down awards.

         This strategy was devised by, implemented by, and maintained at the direction of TGP
         Energy’s former Vice President of Origination (Former Vice President).

         10.    Engaging in this conduct only when LMPs were high was a deliberate effort by
         Terra-Gen (through TGP Energy) to gain the financial benefits of avoiding high-priced
         purchases of energy from the grid when instructed to do so by CAISO. In contrast, the
         Resources did not claim outages or disconnect from automatic generation control when
         they received regulation-up awards, because these awards allowed Terra-Gen (through
         TGP Energy) to profit by selling energy into the grid in real time.

         11.    Taking an outage or disconnecting from automatic generation control in real-time
         was financially beneficial to Terra-Gen (through TGP Energy) when LMPs were high.
         As the Former Vice President explained to his business team, given that Terra-Gen
         (through its relevant subsidiaries) “pa[id] for all the energy” when it was awarded a
         regulation-down award, but was only required to “pay a small amount back” of its day-
         ahead awards when it left the market, it made “sense to keep leaving the market
         whenever [they were] regulated down at high prices.” The Former Vice President
         specifically instructed his team: “If CAISO signals the battery to regulate down in a high
         pricing even[t], we will leave the market, resulting in only a small portion of lost
         revenue.”

         12.   In another contemporaneous email sent to the Former Vice President, a TGP
         Energy employee described this behavior as “leaving and rejoining the market”
         depending on real-time LMPs. Under the Former Vice President’s direction, the TGP
         Energy staff in his business unit kept account of when “CAISO was watching” to decide
         whether to claim outages for the Resources and/or turn off the Resources’ automatic
         generation control connections.

         13.    Enforcement identified 152 hours during the Relevant Period for which Mojave 89
         did not provide regulation-down services as dispatched by CAISO. Terra-Gen identified
         110 hours during the Relevant Period for which Mojave 90 did not provide regulation-
         down services as dispatched; Enforcement confirmed that Mojave 90 did not provide
         those services during those 110 hours.

         14.   By selectively avoiding regulation-down awards during these combined 262 hours,
         Terra-Gen (through its relevant subsidiaries) was unjustly enriched in the total amount of
         $681,007 ($527,480 for Mojave 89 and $153,527 for Mojave 90). This represents Terra-
         Gen’s total net profit during these 262 hours—meaning, total energy and regulation

Document Accession #: 20260407-3069           Filed Date: 04/07/2026

         Docket No. IN26-2-000                                                               -4-

         award payments minus charges incurred for not following CAISO’s regulation-down
         dispatch signals in real time.

                C.     Terra-Gen’s compliance reporting obligations

         15.    In 2021, Terra-Gen reached a settlement with Enforcement in an earlier
         investigation arising from conduct unrelated to this Investigation.4 The Commission-
         approved Stipulation and Consent Agreement (Prior Settlement) required Terra-Gen to:
         (a) pay a civil penalty; (b) make disgorgement; and (c) submit two annual compliance
         monitoring reports to Enforcement. Among other things, these compliance reports were
         required to “identify any known violations of the CAISO Tariff or Commission
         regulations during the applicable period, including a description of the nature of the
         violation and what steps were taken to rectify the situation.”

         16.    On September 1, 2022, Terra-Gen submitted its First Compliance Report to
         Enforcement as required by the Prior Settlement. This Report did not disclose any
         violations of the Tariff associated with Mojave 89.

         17.    However, three months before submitting the First Compliance Report, on June 2,
         2022, the CAISO Market Monitor and the Former Vice President (and members of his
         business unit) had a phone call to discuss the Market Monitor’s concerns related to
         Mojave 89. These concerns involved Mojave 89’s failure to respond to CAISO
         regulation-down awards in the ancillary services market (i.e., the same conduct at issue in
         this Investigation).

         18.     As evidenced by his internal email sent on September 1, 2022, the Former Vice
         President recognized that the Mojave 89 concerns raised by the Market Monitor
         constituted a violation of the Tariff. On the same day (September 1, 2022) that Terra-
         Gen was to submit its First Compliance Report to Enforcement (but before it was
         submitted), the Former Vice President alerted the Terra-Gen personnel responsible for
         assembling the First Compliance Report—including, among others, a Terra-Gen
         executive within the highest levels of the company (High Level Executive)—about the
         Market Monitor’s inquiry into Mojave 89. The Former Vice President wrote in the email
         that, “we did violate the tariff” (referring to the conduct that was the subject of the
         Market Monitor’s prior inquiry). (Emphasis added.) The High Level Executive withheld
         disclosure pending further internal discussion, despite the Prior Settlement requiring that
         it be reported in the First Compliance Report.




                4
                The Commission approved the Stipulation and Consent Agreement in Terra-
         Gen, LLC, 176 FERC ¶ 61,071 (2021).

Document Accession #: 20260407-3069           Filed Date: 04/07/2026

         Docket No. IN26-2-000                                                               -5-

         19.    On September 13, 2022, following a referral from the Market Monitor about the
         practices of Mojave 89 in the ancillary services market, Enforcement sent a document
         preservation notice to Terra-Gen.

         20.    On October 6, 2022, Terra-Gen provided Enforcement with an Amended First
         Compliance Report (Amended Report) that disclosed the Market Monitor’s inquiry into
         Mojave 89. Terra-Gen noted that it had submitted the First Compliance Report on
         September 1, 2022, and stated that “Terra-Gen’s senior management has since confirmed
         that representatives of Terra-Gen’s energy marketing group were contacted by the
         [Market Monitor] in May 2022 regarding the operation of Terra-Gen’s Mojave 89 hybrid
         wind and energy storage resource (Mojave 89 Resource) in the CAISO regulation
         market.” (Emphasis added.) This statement gave Enforcement the misleading
         impression that Terra-Gen did not know about the communications between the Market
         Monitor and the Former Vice President (and his TGP Energy team) until sometime after
         submission of the First Compliance Report. In fact, as discussed above, Terra-Gen
         personnel—including the High Level Executive—knew about the communications before
         the submission.

         21.    Finally, Terra-Gen stated in the Amended Report that its “senior management is in
         the process of determining whether any aspects of the operation of the Mojave 89
         Resource in the regulation market may have violated the CAISO tariff.”

                D.     Terra-Gen’s improved compliance culture

         22.    Since the events giving rise to this Investigation, Terra-Gen has made substantial,
         positive changes to its internal compliance program.

         23.    Among other things, Terra-Gen has:

                a.     Terminated the employment of the Former Vice President who led TGP
                       Energy during the Relevant Period.

                b.     Established an internal energy market compliance function under the charge
                       of the company’s Chief Environment Health & Safety Officer.

                c.     Created a new position of “Director – Energy Markets Compliance,” to
                       oversee internal compliance functions specific to Commission regulations
                       and CAISO requirements (the individual initially holding this position has
                       since been elevated to Senior Director, Compliance & Project
                       Implementation, overseeing two compliance specialists primarily focused
                       on FERC and energy markets compliance).

Document Accession #: 20260407-3069        Filed Date: 04/07/2026

         Docket No. IN26-2-000                                                            -6-

               d.    Created a new position of “FERC EQR Compliance Specialist,” to ensure
                     accurate transactional reporting to the Commission, and tasked this
                     Specialist with reviewing and correcting prior company filings.

               e.    Created a new position of “Compliance Specialist, Energy Markets.”

               f.    Enhanced its policy on reporting suspected violations of Commission
                     regulations and the CAISO Tariff.

               g.    Created a monthly survey that relevant employees (including all members
                     of senior management) are required to take regarding knowledge of any
                     actual or suspected violations of Commission regulations or the CAISO
                     Tariff.

               h.    Established an anonymous reporting tool through a third-party service for
                     employees to report suspected regulatory violations or concerns via a
                     website or hotline.

               i.    Hired outside counsel to conduct annual training (beginning in 2022) for
                     relevant employees on compliance with Part II of the Federal Power Act,
                     the Commission’s regulations, and the company’s FERC Compliance
                     Program Manual.

               j.    Engaged a third-party consultant to administer an in-person compliance
                     training in 2023 with respect to the CAISO market design and participation.
                     This third-party consultant was also engaged to develop annual computer-
                     based training modules for all relevant personnel (i.e., all personnel with
                     market scheduling responsibilities), with respect to CAISO market
                     participation and covering topics that include Commission regulatory
                     requirements. Terra-Gen required the same personnel to undertake a
                     CAISO-created computer-based training regimen on relevant market
                     requirements.

               k.    Updated its internal Code of Ethics to include an emphasized obligation to
                     report any suspected violations of the Code of Ethics and regulatory
                     requirements, and mandated training on the new Code of Ethics for all
                     current employees and all future new hires.

               l.    Engaged another third-party consultant to provide additional CAISO Tariff
                     compliance training, and to conduct a months-long comprehensive internal
                     compliance audit focused on CAISO Tariff compliance, which resulted in a
                     report that identified areas in which Terra-Gen could enhance its practices
                     and procedures, and recommended ways in which to do so.

Document Accession #: 20260407-3069          Filed Date: 04/07/2026

         Docket No. IN26-2-000                                                               -7-

         24.   Terra-Gen has cooperated fully in the Investigation.

         II.   Violations

                Enforcement determined that Terra-Gen’s above-described conduct violated the
         CAISO Tariff, the Commission’s Market Behavior Rule (18 C.F.R § 35.41(a)), the
         Commission’s Duty of Candor Rule (18 C.F.R § 35.41(b)), and the Commission’s Anti-
         Manipulation Rule (18 C.F.R § 1.c.2). Terra-Gen admits all violations except violation
         of the Anti-Manipulation Rule.

               A.     Violations of the CAISO Tariff and the Commission’s Market
                      Behavior and Duty of Candor Rules

                      1.     Violation of CAISO Tariff section 8.75

         26.   CAISO Tariff section 8.7 provides in relevant part: “Once the CAISO has given
         Scheduling Coordinators notice of the Day-Ahead and Real-Time Market Ancillary
         Service Awards and Ancillary Service Schedules, these awards and Schedules represent
         binding commitments made in the markets between the CAISO and the Scheduling
         Coordinators concerned, subject to any amendments issued as described above.”

         27.    Enforcement determined that Terra-Gen (through TGP Energy) violated section
         8.7 by disregarding its “binding commitments.” Instead, Terra-Gen (through its relevant
         subsidiaries) selectively and improperly declared outages for the Resources and/or
         disconnected the Resources from automatic generation control upon receiving regulation-
         down awards from CAISO at a time of high LMPs.

                      2.     Violation of CAISO Tariff section 34.13.16

         28.   CAISO Tariff section 34.13.1 provides in relevant part:

               Resources must:

               a.     unless otherwise stated in the Dispatch Instruction, comply with a
                      Dispatch Instruction immediately upon receipt;

               b.     respond to all Dispatch Instructions in accordance with Good Utility
                      Practice;




               5
                  CAISO, CAISO Tariff, § 8.7 (Ancillary Services Awards) (1.0.0).
               6
                  CAISO, CAISO Tariff, § 34.13.1 (Response Required by Resources to Dispatch
         Instructions) (1.0.0 & 2.0.0).

Document Accession #: 20260407-3069            Filed Date: 04/07/2026

         Docket No. IN26-2-000                                                                 -8-

               c.        meet voltage criteria in accordance with the provision in the CAISO
                         Tariff;

               d.        meet any applicable Operational Ramp Rates;

               e.        respond to Dispatch Instructions for Ancillary Services within the
                         required time periods and (in the case of Participating Generators
                         providing Regulation) respond to [automatic generation control]
                         from the EMS;

               f.        if a time frame is stated in a Dispatch Instruction, respond to a
                         Dispatch Instruction within the stated time frame; and

               g.        not intentionally generate above or below Dispatch Operating Target.

         (Emphasis added.)

         29.    Enforcement determined that Terra-Gen (through TGP Energy) violated section
         34.13.1 by deliberately disregarding certain of CAISO’s dispatch instructions—to wit,
         regulation-down awards during times of high LMPs—and choosing, instead, to declare
         outages and/or disconnect from automatic generation control to avoid paying the high
         prices. In these instances, there was no legitimate basis for taking outages or
         disconnecting the Resources from automatic generation control.

                         3.    Violation of CAISO Tariff section 37.3.1.17

         30.    CAISO Tariff section 37.3.1.1 provides in relevant part: “Market Participants must
         submit Bids for Energy, RUC Capacity and Ancillary Services and Submissions to Self-
         Provide an Ancillary Service from resources that are reasonably expected to be available
         and capable of performing at the levels specified in the Bid, and to remain available and
         capable of so performing based on all information that is known to the Market Participant
         or should have been known to the Market Participant at the time of submission.”

         31.    Enforcement determined that Terra-Gen (through TGP Energy) violated section
         37.3.1.1. by submitting bids in the day-ahead market with full knowledge that it planned
         to make the Resources unavailable in the real-time market (by declaring outages and/or
         disconnecting from automatic generation control) if CAISO made a regulation-down
         award when LMPs were high.




               7
                    CAISO, CAISO Tariff, § 37.3.1.1 (Expected Conduct) (3.0.0).

Document Accession #: 20260407-3069          Filed Date: 04/07/2026

         Docket No. IN26-2-000                                                              -9-

                      4.     Violation of 18 C.F.R. § 35.41(a)

         32.    The Commission’s Market Behavior Rule, 18 C.F.R. § 35.41(a), requires Sellers
         to “operate and schedule generating facilities . . . declare outages, and commit or
         otherwise bid supply in a manner that complies with the Commission-approved rules and
         regulations of the applicable market.”

         33.    Enforcement determined that Terra-Gen (through its subsidiaries) did not operate
         the Resources, declare outages, or bid supply “in a manner that complies with the
         Commission-approved rules and regulations of the applicable market.” In particular,
         Enforcement determined that Terra-Gen (through TGP Energy) disregarded certain of its
         obligations as a participant in CAISO’s ancillary services market, including the
         obligation to respond to all CAISO regulation-down awards through automatic generation
         control in real time. Enforcement determined that Terra-Gen (through TGP Energy)
         violated its obligations by selectively claiming unjustified outages and removing the
         Resources from automatic generation control when doing so advanced its financial
         interests.

                      5.     Violation of 18 C.F.R. § 35.41(b)

         34.     Enforcement also determined that Terra-Gen (through its subsidiaries) violated
         the Commission’s Duty of Candor Rule, 18 C.F.R. § 35.41(b), which requires a Seller to
         “provide accurate and factual information and not submit false or misleading information,
         or omit material information, in any communication with the Commission . . . unless
         Seller exercises due diligence to prevent such occurrences.” Enforcement found that
         Terra-Gen violated this provision as follows:

               a.     Terra-Gen violated 18 C.F.R. § 35.41(b) by omission in its First
                      Compliance Report. As noted above, pursuant to the Prior Settlement,
                      Terra-Gen was obligated to report “any known violations of the CAISO
                      Tariff or Commission regulations during the applicable period.” The
                      Former Vice President wrote in an internal email sent on September 1,
                      2022, that Terra-Gen had violated the Tariff in connection with the conduct
                      identified in the Market Monitor’s inquiry. This email was sent to, among
                      others, the High Level Executive, who signed and verified under oath the
                      First Compliance Report. This email was sent a few hours before Terra-
                      Gen submitted the First Compliance Report to Enforcement. However,
                      Terra-Gen did not include the information in that Report.

               b.     Terra-Gen stated in its First Compliance Report that it “ha[d] not received
                      notice of other violations of the CAISO Tariff or the Commission’s
                      regulations during the applicable period.” Enforcement determined this
                      was misleading in light of the information that Terra-Gen had received
                      prior to submission of the First Compliance Report.

Document Accession #: 20260407-3069          Filed Date: 04/07/2026

         Docket No. IN26-2-000                                                              - 10 -

               c.     In the Amended Report, Terra-Gen stated that it had submitted the First
                      Compliance Report on September 1, 2022 and that its “senior management
                      had since confirmed that representatives of Terra-Gen’s energy marketing
                      group were contacted by the [Market Monitor] in May 2022 regarding the
                      operation of Terra-Gen’s Mojave 89 hybrid wind and energy storage
                      resource . . ..” (Emphasis added.) Enforcement determined this was
                      misleading, because the Market Monitor had contacted Terra-Gen in May
                      2022 and a member of Terra-Gen’s senior management (the High Level
                      Executive) was aware of this hours before submitting the First Compliance
                      Report. For example, in the same September 1, 2022 email in which he
                      stated that a violation of the Tariff had occurred, the Former Vice President
                      forwarded the Market Monitor’s initial May 19, 2022 inquiry about the
                      matter and acknowledged his participation in a prior call with the Market
                      Monitor to discuss the Market Monitor’s inquiry into Mojave 89. This
                      prior call occurred in June 2022, long before the submission of the First
                      Compliance Report.

                      Thus, by September 1, 2022, and prior to submitting the First Compliance
                      Report, the High Level Executive and other Terra-Gen personnel
                      responsible for assembling and submitting the First Compliance Report,
                      knew about the prior inquiry made by the Market Monitor. Indeed, in an
                      internal email sent on September 1, 2022, before submitting the First
                      Compliance Report to Enforcement, the High Level Executive (a)
                      acknowledged the Market Monitor’s prior inquiry into Mojave 89, but (b)
                      stated that Terra-Gen had a plan to not disclose the inquiry to Enforcement
                      in the First Compliance Report and, instead, supplement later if the Market
                      Monitor pursued the issue.

               d.     Last, Terra-Gen stated in its Amended Report that “senior management is
                      in the process of determining whether any aspects of the operation of the
                      Mojave 89 Resource in the regulation market may have violated the CAISO
                      tariff.” (Emphasis added.) Enforcement determined this also was
                      misleading, because before submitting the First Compliance Report, the
                      Former Vice President had plainly stated in the September 1 email that
                      Terra-Gen had violated the Tariff. Even if others at Terra-Gen did not take
                      his statement at face value, the Former Vice President’s statement qualified
                      as reason enough to believe that Terra-Gen “may” have violated the Tariff.

         35.   Enforcement determined that Terra-Gen did not exercise due diligence in
         connection with these misstatements and omissions.

Document Accession #: 20260407-3069             Filed Date: 04/07/2026

         Docket No. IN26-2-000                                                                  - 11 -

                B.     Violation of Section 222 of the Federal Power Act and the
                       Commission’s Anti-Manipulation Rule

         36.    Section 222 of the Federal Power Act (16 U.S.C. § 824v) and the Commission’s
         Anti-Manipulation Rule promulgated thereunder (18 C.F.R. § 1c.2) broadly prohibit
         fraudulent and manipulative practices within the nation’s interstate electricity markets. In
         relevant part, the Rule provides: “It shall be unlawful for any entity, directly or indirectly,
         in connection with the purchase or sale of electric energy . . . subject to the jurisdiction of
         the Commission,” to “employ any device, scheme, or artifice to defraud,” or to “engage
         in any act, practice, or course of business that operates or would operate as a fraud or
         deceit upon any entity.”

         37.    Enforcement determined that Terra-Gen (through TGP Energy) engaged in a
         “scheme,” “practice, or course of business” during the Relevant Period that operated as a
         fraud on CAISO and its ancillary services market. As detailed above, the Former Vice
         President developed a strategy consisting of selectively exiting the CAISO real-time
         ancillary services market by declaring outages for the Resources and/or disconnecting the
         Resources from automatic generation control if—and only if—CAISO directed Terra-
         Gen (through TGP Energy) to purchase electricity from the grid (through a regulation-
         down award) at a time of high LMPs. The Former Vice President directed the employees
         under his supervision to engage in the manipulative conduct.

         38.     This scheme included bidding for ancillary services in the day-ahead market with
         the intention of submitting illegitimate outages and/or disconnecting from automatic
         generation control in unfavorable economic conditions. By selectively participating in
         the ancillary services market—that is, by reaping the profits of regulation-up awards and
         simultaneously avoiding regulation-down awards when the LMPs were high—Terra-Gen
         (through TGP Energy) was able to maximize its profits and minimize or eliminate the
         risks that are naturally attendant to participation in the CAISO ancillary services market.

         39.     Terra-Gen (through TGP Energy) received more than $680,000 in unjust profits
         from CAISO, but refused to deliver in real-time when economic conditions did not suit
         its financial interests.

         40.    Enforcement determined that the evidence, moreover, demonstrates that Terra-Gen
         (through TGP Energy) acted with the intention of defrauding the market, i.e., with
         scienter. The Former Vice President calculated that Terra-Gen would make more money
         by offering bids into the day-ahead market, and then avoiding regulation-down awards in
         the real-time market through unjustified outages and/or disconnecting from automatic
         generation control, as opposed to complying with the Tariff and fulfilling all ancillary
         services awards under all conditions. The Former Vice President directed his team via
         email to engage in this unlawful scheme: “If CAISO signals the battery to regulate down

Document Accession #: 20260407-3069            Filed Date: 04/07/2026

         Docket No. IN26-2-000                                                                 - 12 -

         in a high pricing even[t], we will leave the market, resulting in only a small portion of
         lost revenue.”

         41.    Enforcement determined that additional evidence that Terra-Gen acted with
         scienter is provided by contemporaneous internal emails demonstrating that the Former
         Vice President and his team would not engage in the scheme if they believed that CAISO
         was “watching.” For example, in an email sent to the Former Vice President on July 10,
         2021, a member of his business team reported that Terra-Gen had incurred several
         thousands of dollars in losses as a result of a CAISO regulation-down award. This
         employee explained that because “CAISO was carefully watching our battery,” the team
         “did not have much opportunity to leave the market to prevent” the losses. Enforcement
         determined that this evidence proves that Terra-Gen (through certain TGP Energy
         personnel) knew that its actions were in violation of Commission regulations and/or the
         CAISO Tariff and actively took steps to avoid detection.

         42.     Last, the CAISO ancillary services market is a Commission-regulated interstate
         market that is subject to the Commission-approved Tariff, and, therefore, the
         manipulative conduct described herein was carried out “in connection with the purchase
         or sale of electric energy . . . subject to the jurisdiction of the Commission.”

         III.   Stipulation and Consent Agreement

                Enforcement and Terra-Gen have resolved the Investigation by means of the
         attached Agreement.

                Terra-Gen stipulates to the facts set forth in section II of the Agreement, admits
         the violations described in section III.A of the Agreement, and neither admits nor denies
         the violations described in section III.B of the Agreement.

                Terra-Gen agrees to pay a civil penalty of $4,950,000 to the United States

                                         194 FERC ¶ 61,029
                                    UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                           FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

         Before Commissioners: Laura V. Swett, Chairman;
                               David Rosner, Lindsay S. See,
                               Judy W. Chang, and David LaCerte.

         Tenaska Power Services Co.                                   Docket No. IN25-13-000

                   ORDER APPROVING STIPULATION AND CONSENT AGREEMENT

                                        (Issued January 12, 2026)

         1.      The Commission approves the attached Stipulation and Consent Agreement
         (Agreement) between the Office of Enforcement and Regulatory Accounting
         (Enforcement) and Tenaska Power Services Co. (TPS). This order is in the public
         interest because the Agreement resolves on fair and equitable terms Enforcement’s
         investigation (Investigation) under Part 1b of the Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R.
         Part 1b (2025), into whether TPS violated the ISO New England Inc. (ISO-NE) Open
         Access Transmission Tariff (Tariff) and the Commission’s regulations while submitting
         offers for the output from an approximately 250 MW natural gas-fired generator in
         Agawam, Massachusetts (the Berkshire Generator) on January 11-12, 2021 (the Relevant
         Period).1

         2.     TPS stipulates to the facts set forth in Section II of the Agreement, but neither
         admits nor denies the alleged violations in Section III of the Agreement. TPS agrees to
         (a) pay a civil penalty of $51,000 to the United States Treasury; (b) disgorge $78,354,
         plus interest, to ISO-NE; and (c) provide compliance monitoring reports to Enforcement
         as provided in the Agreement.

         I.    Facts

         3.      During the Relevant Period, TPS served as the Lead Market Participant in ISO-NE
         for the Energy and Ancillary Services from the Berkshire Generator. As Lead Market
         Participant, TPS was required to submit offers on behalf of the Berkshire Generator
         (including all information necessary to submit such offers) and to respond to ISO-NE’s


               1
                During the Relevant Period, the Berkshire Generator was owned by Berkshire
         Power Company LLC (Berkshire Power). Berkshire Power was subsequently sold in
         September 2024. See Berkshire Power Co., LLC, 188 FERC ¶ 62,137 (2024).

Document Accession #: 20260112-3012              Filed Date: 01/12/2026

         Docket No. IN25-13-000                                                                 -2-

         directives to start, shutdown, or change output. TPS is authorized by the Commission to
         sell power at market-based rates.2

         4.    During the Relevant Period, the Berkshire Generator had an ISO-NE Capacity
         Supply Obligation (CSO) of 229 MW.

         5.     The owner of the Berkshire Generator during the Relevant Period, Berkshire
         Power, as noted above, was an affiliate of TPS. During the Relevant Period, Berkshire
         Power compensated TPS for performing the duties of Lead Market Participant on behalf
         of the Berkshire Generator’s Energy and Ancillary Services in the ISO-NE energy
         markets.

         6.     In consultation with Berkshire Power and plant operators, TPS procured natural
         gas fuel for the Berkshire Generator through requests to an affiliated fuel supplier,
         Tenaska Marketing Ventures (Tenaska Marketing).

         7.      During the Relevant Period, TPS submitted day-ahead and real-time energy offers
         for the Berkshire Generator and accepted the other obligations under ISO-NE’s tariff
         applicable to Lead Market Participants. Under ISO-NE Tariff Section III.1.7.20(b), Lead
         Market Participants are responsible for submitting energy offers from generators
         (including the physical operating characteristics of the generators), updating such offers,
         and communicating the availability and unavailability of generators for which they
         submit offers.

         8.     The Economic Maximum (EcoMax) is one of the physical parameters for a
         generator that must be communicated to ISO-NE. A generator’s EcoMax is the
         maximum available output that a Market Participant offers to supply. A Market
         Participant must maintain an up-to-date EcoMax for all hours in which the Generator
         Asset has been offered.3

         9.     In addition, resources with CSOs have “strict performance obligations.”4
         Specifically, under ISO-NE Tariff Section III.13.6.1.1.1, resources must “offer into both
         the day-ahead and real-time energy markets a MW amount equal to or greater than [the]
         Capacity Supply Obligation when the resource is physically available.” Under ISO-NE
         Tariff Section III.1.10.1A(c)(v), resources with CSOs must also “keep supply offers open
                2
                 See Tenaska Power Servs. Co., Docket No. ER94-389-000 (May 26, 1994)
         (unreported).
                3
                    See ISO-NE Tariff § I.2.2.
                4
                See New England Power Generators Association, Inc. v. ISO New England Inc.,
         144 FERC ¶ 61,157 at P 55 (NEPGA), order on reh’g, 145 FERC ¶ 61,206 (2013).

Document Accession #: 20260112-3012           Filed Date: 01/12/2026

         Docket No. IN25-13-000                                                               -3-

         throughout the operating day.”5 During the Relevant Period, as Lead Market Participant
         for a Capacity Resource, TPS was offering energy from its affiliated Capacity Resource.

         10.    In exchange for being offered into the ISO-NE energy markets on a daily basis,
         resources with CSOs receive monthly capacity payments. During January 2021,
         Berkshire Power’s monthly capacity payment was approximately $1,214,490.

         11.     The Commission has found that the ISO-NE tariff excuses performance by a
         resource with a CSO where the resource is physically unavailable due to its inability to
         procure fuel or transportation for the resource to run beyond its day-ahead commitment,
         or when not scheduled in the day-ahead market.6 An economic decision not to procure
         fuel (e.g., where fuel has become more expensive after an offer is submitted) does not
         excuse a lack of performance.7

         12.    On Saturday, January 9, 2021, TPS submitted a Day-Ahead energy offer to
         ISO-NE for Monday, January 11, 2021 for the Berkshire Generator with an EcoMax of
         251 MW. On January 10, 2021, ISO-NE notified TPS that the Berkshire Generator had
         received a day-ahead award at its EcoMax for every hour of January 11, 2021.

         13.   On January 11, 2021, TPS submitted Day-Ahead energy offers for January 12,
         2021 for the Berkshire Generator with an identical EcoMax of 251 MW. Also on
         January 11, ISO-NE notified TPS that the Berkshire Generator had received a day-ahead
         award at its EcoMax for every hour of January 12, 2021.

         14.    ISO-NE dispatched the Berkshire Generator on January 11, 2021, consistent with
         its day-ahead award. On January 11, the Berkshire Generator initially operated and
         produced energy at its full EcoMax of 251 MW.

         15.    Shortly after 10:00 am on January 11, 2021, after the Berkshire Generator received
         its day-ahead award for January 11, but before it received its day-ahead award for
         January 12, Tennessee Gas Pipeline (the natural gas pipeline serving the Berkshire
         Generator) issued an Operational Flow Order (OFO) affecting the meter connected to the
         Berkshire Generator. After Berkshire Power informed TPS of the OFO issued to
         Berkshire, and that the OFO indicated that planned natural gas fuel deliveries to the
         Berkshire Generator could be impacted, TPS understood that additional fuel supplies
         would need to be secured for the generator to operate at its EcoMax.

               6

               7
                   Id.

Document Accession #: 20260112-3012             Filed Date: 01/12/2026

         Docket No. IN25-13-000                                                                -4-

         16.     Following the issuance of the OFO, TPS, working with Tenaska Marketing,
         immediately attempted to locate additional intraday supplies of natural gas to make up for
         the expected reduction of scheduled gas deliveries to the Berkshire Generator. TPS
         learned that additional intraday non-firm gas supplies could be obtained to operate the
         Berkshire Generator at its dispatched EcoMax, but that the prices for those fuel supplies
         would be elevated. TPS advised Berkshire Power and plant operators of the fuel supply
         situation. At that time, Berkshire Power did not authorize TPS to purchase additional
         fuel.

         17.    Berkshire Power personnel subsequently contacted the ISO-NE control room and
         requested to reduce the dispatch of the Berkshire Generator from 251 MW to 150 MW
         (an amount that was below both the Berkshire Generator’s EcoMax and CSO). Berkshire
         Power personnel did not mention that fuel was available to operate the Berkshire
         Generator at full EcoMax and at the CSO.

         18.    With Berkshire Power personnel’s knowledge, ISO-NE personnel then placed the
         Berkshire Generator into a “limited-energy generator” (LEG) status with a maximum
         physical output equal to 150 MW. LEG status is limited to generators that, due to
         physical design considerations or environmental restrictions, are unable to operate
         continuously at full output on a daily basis.8 However, the Berkshire Generator did not
         qualify for LEG status. Immediately following the communications between Berkshire
         personnel and ISO-NE, ISO-NE began sending reduced dispatch instructions to the
         Berkshire Generator, dropping the dispatch requirement from the unit’s EcoMax to its
         EcoMin, and the Berkshire Generator reduced its output accordingly, from 251 MW to
         150 MW.

         19.      Early on January 12, 2021, the pipeline supplying gas to the Berkshire Generator
         removed the OFO condition. At 6:36 AM, a Berkshire Generator operator contacted the
         ISO-NE Operations Control Room to request that the generator be dispatched back up to
         its full day-ahead EcoMax award of 251 MW. During the call, the ISO-NE Control
         Room operator asked for, and received, confirmation that the Berkshire Generator
         operator was requesting that ISO-NE remove the LEG designation. ISO-NE then
         resumed dispatch of the Berkshire Generator at its full EcoMax.

         20.   The Investigation arose out of a referral from ISO-NE’s Internal Market Monitor.

         21.   TPS fully cooperated with Enforcement during the Investigation.

                   See ISO-NE Tariff § I.2.2.

Document Accession #: 20260112-3012           Filed Date: 01/12/2026

         Docket No. IN25-13-000                                                                 -5-

         II.    Violations

         22.     Enforcement determined that during the Relevant Period, TPS violated provisions
         of the ISO-NE tariff and 18 C.F.R. §§ 35.41(a) and (b) when its affiliate, Berkshire
         Power, sought to avoid additional more expensive fuel purchases that would have
         enabled the Berkshire Generator, an ISO-NE capacity resource, to run at the levels
         dispatched by ISO-NE per the resource’s day ahead award.

         23.     Resources in ISO-NE with CSOs have a strict performance obligation. Capacity
         resources receive guaranteed monthly capacity payments in exchange for which they are
         required to be offered into the ISO-NE energy markets on a daily basis and to be
         available for operation regardless of whether a daily offer is accepted. Nonperformance
         by or inaccurate information about these resources can have substantial economic and
         reliability effects.

         24.    Section III.13.6.1.1.1 of the ISO-NE Tariff requires Generating Capacity
         Resources, like the Berkshire Generator resource, to “be offered into both the Day-Ahead
         Energy Market and Real-Time Energy Market at a MW amount equal to or greater than
         its Capacity Supply Obligation whenever the resource is physically available . . . .”

         25.     ISO-NE Tariff Section III.13.6.1.1.2 requires that Day-Ahead and Real-Time
         Energy Market offers “reflect the then-known unit-specific operating characteristics
         (taking into account, among other things, the physical design characteristics of the unit)
         consistent with Good Utility Practice. Resources must re-declare to the ISO any changes
         to the offer parameters that occur in real time to reflect the known capability of the
         resource.”

         26.    In NEPGA, 144 FERC ¶ 61,157 at P 47, the Commission held that the ISO-NE
         Tariff establishes “a strict performance obligation on capacity resources and that capacity
         resources may not take economic outages, including outages based on economic
         decisions not to procure fuel or transportation.”

         27.     Enforcement determined that TPS violated Sections III.13.6.1.1.1 and
         III.13.6.1.1.2 of the ISO-NE Tariff during the Relevant Period by modifying the real-time
         offers of the Berkshire Generator based on economic factors rather than physical
         availability. Further, even if such a revised offer was permitted, TPS did not ascertain
         whether LEG status was appropriate for the plant and did not dispute, through Berkshire
         Power, LEG status for which the Berkshire Generator was ineligible. The effect of these
         actions was to enable Berkshire Power to take an economic outage inconsistent with the
         performance obligation of resources with CSOs.

         28.     Section 35.41(a) of the Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R. § 35.41(a), provides
         that: “[w]here a Seller participates in a Commission-approved organized market, Seller
         must operate and schedule generating facilities, undertake maintenance, declare outages,

Document Accession #: 20260112-3012            Filed Date: 01/12/2026

         Docket No. IN25-13-000                                                                    -6-

         and commit or otherwise bid supply in a manner that complies with the Commission-
         approved rules and regulations of the applicable market.” Section 35.36(a)(1) of the
         Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R. § 35.36(a)(1), defines “Seller” as “any person that
         has authorization to or seeks authorization to engage in sales for resale of electric energy,
         capacity or ancillary services at market-based rates under section 205 of the Federal
         Power Act.”

         29.     TPS has, and had during the Relevant Period, market-based rate authorization and
         failed to schedule the Berkshire Generator consistent with the ISO-NE Tariff, as
         described above. Enforcement therefore concluded that TPS violated 18 C.F.R.
         § 35.41(a).

         30.     Section 35.41(b) of the Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R. § 35.41(b), provides
         that: “[a] Seller must provide accurate and factual information and not submit false or
         misleading information, or omit material information, in any communication with the
         Commission, Commission-approved market monitors, Commission-approved regional
         transmission organizations, Commission-approved independent system operators, or
         jurisdictional transmission providers, unless Seller exercises due diligence to prevent
         such occurrences.”

         31.    Enforcement determined that attempts to reduce the dispatched level of the
         Berkshire Generator resource falsely and misleadingly communicated to ISO-NE a
         physical inability to operate at the resource’s CSO. These false communications violated
         18 C.F.R. § 35.41(b) because such a reduction was not due to a physical inability to
         operate but rather an economic decision not to procure higher-priced fuel.

         III.   Stipulation and Consent Agreement

         32.  Enforcement and TPS have resolved the Investigation by means of the attached
         Agreement.

         33.   TPS stipulates to the facts set forth in Section II of the Agreement, but neither
         admits nor denies the violations described in Section III of the Agreement.

         34.    TPS agrees to pay a civil penalty of $51,000 to the United States Treasury.

         35.    TPS agrees to pay $78,354, plus interest, in disgorgement to ISO-NE.

         36.   TPS agrees to submit an annual compliance monitoring report to Enforcement for
         one year with the second year at Enforcement’s discretion.

Document Accession #: 20260112-3012            Filed Date: 01/12/2026

         Docket No. IN25-13-000                                                                   -7-

         IV.    Determination of Appropriate Remedies and Sanctions

        37.    In recommending the appropriate remedy, Enforcement considered the factors
        described in the Revised Policy Statement on Penalty Guidelines,9 including that TPS
        cooperated with Enforcement during the Investigation.

         38.    The Commission concludes that the Agreement is a fair and equitable resolution of
         the matters concerned and is in the public interest, as it reflects the nature and seriousness
         of the conduct and recognizes the specific considerations stated above and in the
         Agreement.

         39.   The Commission also concludes that TPS’s civil penalty is consistent with the
         Revised Policy Statement on Penalty Guidelines.10

         40.    The Commission directs TPS to make the civil penalty payment and disgorgement
         as required by the Agreement within twenty days after the Effective Date of the
         Agreement.

         41.   The Commission directs ISO-NE to allocate the disgorgement funds as set forth in
         the Agreement.

         The Commission orders:

               The attached Stipulation and Consent Agreement is hereby approved without
         modification.

         By the Commission.

         (SEAL)

                                                              Secretary.

            12.   On Saturday, January 9, 2021, TPS submitted a Day-Ahead energy offer to ISO-NE
            for Monday, January 11, 2021 for the Berkshire Generator with an EcoMax of 251 MW.
            On January 10, 2021, ISO-NE notified TPS that the Berkshire Generator had received a
            day-ahead award at its EcoMax for every hour of January 11, 2021.

            13.    On January 11, 2021, TPS submitted Day-Ahead energy offers for January 12, 2021
            for the Berkshire Generator with an identical EcoMax of 251 MW. Also on January 11,
            ISO-NE notified TPS that the Berkshire Generator had received a day-ahead award at its
            EcoMax for every hour of January 12, 2021.

            14.    ISO-NE dispatched the Berkshire Generator on January 11, 2021, consistent with
            its day-ahead award. On January 11, the Berkshire Generator initially operated and
            produced energy at its full EcoMax of 251 MW.

            15.    Shortly after 10:00 am on January 11, 2021, after the Berkshire Generator received
            its day-ahead award for January 11, but before it received its day-ahead award for January
            12, Tennessee Gas Pipeline (the natural gas pipeline serving the Berkshire Generator)
            issued an Operational Flow Order (OFO) affecting the meter connected to the Berkshire
            Generator. After Berkshire Power informed TPS of the OFO issued to Berkshire, and that
            the OFO indicated that planned natural gas fuel deliveries to the Berkshire Generator could
            be impacted, TPS understood that additional fuel supplies would need to be secured for the
            generator to operate at its EcoMax.

            16.    Following the issuance of the OFO, TPS, working with Tenaska Marketing,
            immediately attempted to locate additional intraday supplies of natural gas to make up for
            the expected reduction of scheduled gas deliveries to the Berkshire Generator. TPS learned

            III.   VIOLATIONS

            22.     Enforcement determined that during the Relevant Period, TPS violated provisions
            of the ISO-NE tariff and 18 C.F.R. §§ 35.41(a) and (b) when its affiliate, Berkshire Power,
            sought to avoid additional more expensive fuel purchases that would have enabled the
            Berkshire Generator, an ISO-NE capacity resource, to run at the levels dispatched by ISO-
            NE per the resource’s day ahead award.

            23.    Resources in ISO-NE with CSOs have a strict performance obligation. Capacity
            resources receive guaranteed monthly capacity payments in exchange for which they are
            required to be offered into the ISO-NE energy markets on a daily basis and to be available

         24.     Section III.13.6.1.1.1 of the ISO-NE Tariff requires Generating Capacity Resources,

         Market and Real-Time Energy Market at a MW amount equal to or greater than its Capacity

         25.    ISO-NE Tariff Section III.13.6.1.1.2 requires that Day-Ahead and Real-Time
         Energy Market offers “reflect the then-known unit-specific operating characteristics
         (taking into account, among other things, the physical design characteristics of the unit)

         26.    In NEPGA, 144 FERC ¶ 61,157 at P 47, the Commission held that the ISO-NE Tariff

         resources may not take economic outages, including outages based on economic decisions
         not to procure fuel or transportation.”

         27.    Enforcement determined that TPS violated Sections III.13.6.1.1.1 and III.13.6.1.1.2
         of the ISO-NE Tariff during the Relevant Period by modifying the real-time offers of the
         Berkshire Generator based on economic factors rather than physical availability. Further,
         even if such a revised offer was permitted, TPS did not ascertain whether LEG status was
         appropriate for the plant and did not dispute, through Berkshire Power, LEG status for
         which the Berkshire Generator was ineligible. The effect of these actions was to enable
         Berkshire Power to take an economic outage inconsistent with the performance obligation
         of resources with CSOs.

         28.     Section 35.41(a) of the Commission’s regulations, 18 C.F.R. § 35.41(a), provides

         29.     TPS has, and had during the Relevant Period, market-based rate authorization and
         failed to schedule the Berkshire Generator consistent with the ISO-NE Tariff, as described
